selected_evidence.requirement: Inventory application served over TCP port 8181 with SELinux enforcing (pre-restart)
selected_evidence.summary: Baseline showed SELinux Enforcing and no web server; httpd was installed, configured to Listen on 8181, given the http_port_t SELinux port label, started, firewall-opened, and verified serving the inventory page content with no AVC denials, all while getenforce reported Enforcing.
Captured boot_id (7223d5b7-fa56-4ff3-acee-959a5cf5f146), uptime, SELinux Enforcing, httpd active, port 8181 listening, and correct app content before the restart.

selected_evidence.requirement: Node1 restart acknowledgement returned before disconnect
selected_evidence.summary: systemd-run scheduled a deferred reboot and returned its acknowledgement (timer/service unit names) before the connection dropped.
Poll attempts timed out and then saw connection reset, consistent with the node rebooting.

selected_evidence.requirement: Proof of changed boot identity after restart
selected_evidence.summary: Post-reboot poll succeeded and returned a new boot_id (86692ec5-2a0d-46a8-8841-d538dc542eeb) and new uptime (08:25:15), differing from the pre-restart baseline, proving the node actually rebooted rather than just becoming reachable again.

selected_evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of required services/data and continued SELinux enforcement
selected_evidence.summary: After the restart, SELinux is still Enforcing, httpd is active with fresh PIDs, port 8181 is listening, the firewall rule persisted, the inventory app returns correct content, and no AVC denials were found.
